analyst_view.overall: Le Mans are 17th, in the last relegation spot, and haven't won in four league games. Monaco are seventh but have dropped points in four straight league games, and they played a Conference League tie on Thursday (a 2-0 win over Nordsjaelland). Le Mans are without Adil Bourabaa until early 2027. One preview says Ansu Fati and Stanis Idumbo are only doubts, not certain absentees.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Monaco have scored only once in their last two away league games, and one report says they wasted plenty of chances again on Thursday. Le Mans are missing their main creative outlet, Bourabaa, and Filipe Luis may rotate after the European trip, so we expect a tighter game than the model does.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.0 corners. Nothing in the team news changes the picture: Monaco should have more of the ball, and Le Mans have been reasonably competitive at home, taking points in three of four home games.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, which is already high. One preview calls Le Mans "a little over-aggressive at the back", and as a side fighting relegation and chasing Monaco's possession, they should be giving away fouls. Bastien Dechepy is the referee. We'd sooner go above the model's number than below it.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots. Monaco take a lot of shots even when they struggle to score, and Le Mans shoot more at home, so we see no strong reason to move away from the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. With Monaco's finishing off form and Le Mans missing Bourabaa, more of the shots look likely to be blocked or off target, so we lean slightly lower.
